usageNotes: Creates a point-in-time snapshot of a QEMU VM; the operation is asynchronous and returns a UPID task string that must be polled via the tasks API to confirm completion. The VM can be running or stopped — if running, set vmstate to true to also capture RAM state (required for a fully live, restorable snapshot; omitting it saves disk space but loses in-memory state). The caller must hold VM.Snapshot permission on /vms/{vmid}.

examples.summary: Snapshot a running VM with RAM state before a risky change

tips: snapname must match the pve-configid format: alphanumeric plus hyphens/underscores, max 40 chars — do not use dots or spaces.
vmstate snapshots are significantly larger (VM RAM size added to snapshot) and take longer to create and restore.
Poll the returned UPID with get_nodes_node_tasks_upid_status to detect failures; the POST returns immediately even if the snapshot job is still running.
Snapshots are stored inline with the VM disk on the same storage — ensure the datastore has enough free space before snapshotting, especially with vmstate enabled.
The reserved snapshot name 'current' is used internally by Proxmox to represent the live state; do not use it as a snapname.
